units.text: Let's follow audio into a transcript and text back into speech. Transcribe accepts supported audio recordings or streams and produces timestamped text. Language identification and redaction are options for supported workloads, not proof that all sensitive words are gone.

Captioning needs timing, while search and contact-center analysis use the text for different work. Verify enough of the actual transcript for the task. A word-detection error can change the meaning even if the output sounds plausible.

Polly does the reverse: give it text or supported speech markup and it returns audio. A pronunciation lexicon lets you guide how supported words or names are spoken. Test the chosen voice and language rather than assuming all markup works with every engine.

Translate takes text in one supported language and returns text in another. For this product description, provide the appropriate terminology, then have a reviewer check it in context. Accurate words alone don't guarantee the intended brand or local meaning.

Connect routes a contact through its flow. Lex can recognize the caller's intent and collect the details needed for a self-service answer. If the flow can't resolve the request, it can transfer it to an agent. The bot handles a dialog; it doesn't replace contact routing and ownership.

We'll decide how to build and operate a custom model. Start with representative data, train and evaluate, then choose an inference mode that fits the traffic. SageMaker AI provides managed tools for those steps; you still own the model decisions.

If you need a model trained or hosted according to your own requirements, compare the SageMaker AI workflow. If the job can use a managed foundation model through an A P I, compare Bedrock. Neither path removes the need to measure output quality and access.

Use held-out data to decide whether to register and promote a candidate model. If it fails the release gate, improve the inputs or training rather than shipping a model based only on training accuracy.

After deployment, watch performance and data drift. A change in the real input can degrade a model that once passed. Compare against the release criteria and retrain when there is evidence it will improve performance.

For the inventory example, define the target, horizon and accuracy you need first. Forecast is closed to new customers, while existing customers can continue eligible use. For a new workload, evaluate a supported SageMaker forecasting option, then validate it on the actual time series.

We'll choose managed services by the result the application needs. Kendra can index authorized sources for existing customers. It is no longer open to new customers. For a new retrieval or grounded-answer design, evaluate a current Bedrock managed knowledge base and verify access and relevance.

Personalize uses item and user-interaction data to generate recommendations. A recent interaction can be a useful signal, but cold-start users may have little history. Verify data quality and measure recommendations against a useful outcome, not just whether a response comes back.

Textract can extract structured content such as form fields or table cells. In this invoice example, verify that the amount is tied to the intended label, not just present somewhere in recognized text. Route uncertain or consequential values to an appropriate review.

Now compare the outputs: a document field, spoken audio, a conversational intent, and a recommendation all call for different services. Check availability and rights to use the data before building; a legacy option listed on a comparison isn't automatically available to a new account.

We'll follow a foundation model request and then add retrieval. Start with a supported model for the content and quality you need. The application calls Bedrock under scoped permissions. Optional content safeguards help enforce policy, but they don't certify the answer.

Measure actual response quality, latency and cost. Check data handling and where inference is allowed. If the application needs evidence from internal documents, connect a retrieval design rather than hoping the model already knows it.

A permitted application sends the request to the configured model or inference profile. Verify the selected model, Region and allowed destinations if the profile can route beyond one Region. Apply any configured input guardrail at the intended step.

Apply configured output checks and handle the result. A P I audit records and model invocation content logging are distinct. If you enable content logging, limit who can access it and avoid collecting sensitive material unnecessarily.

Before a user asks anything, take approved documents, break them into useful chunks and make representations that can be searched. Store those with metadata. Keep track of changes and deletions; stale indexed text can still be found.

At query time, retrieve relevant passages the caller is allowed to use. Then give the model that evidence and return references where supported. A convincing answer doesn't compensate for missing or unauthorized evidence.

Compare the guided vector-store setup with connecting a supported store you already operate. The decision affects who controls configuration, capacity, security and lifecycle. Verify which connectors and access features the exact option supports.

Access to the knowledge base A P I doesn't mean access to every document. Use supported document controls where configured, or enforce an appropriate retrieval boundary in the application. Test with users who should see different documents.

When an approved source changes, verify ingestion or sync completes. Check the index version and see which passage the application actually retrieves. A fresh source file doesn't prove the index and answer are fresh.

When evidence is missing, outdated, conflicting or unauthorized, don't invent a grounded answer. Use the safe no-answer or review path. Evaluate retrieval relevance separately from whether the final answer faithfully uses what was retrieved.
